history.dynasty: Ahluwalia (Kapurthala State); built by Sardar Fateh Singh Ahluwalia
history.period: Early 19th century (Fateh Singh became Ahluwalia chief in 1801; died October 1836)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is actually in KAPURTHALA town, about 21 km from Jalandhar - the CSV town 'Jalandhar' is approximate (Jalandhar is the reference city). The Panch Mandir is a famous temple complex of five small temples dedicated to several Hindu gods and goddesses, built by Sardar Fateh Singh Ahluwalia, founder of the Kapurthala State. Fateh Singh (d. October 1836) was the chosen companion of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, commanded in the Bhimbar, Rajauri and Bahawalpur expeditions, and in 1806 acted as Ranjit Singh's plenipotentiary signing the first Anglo-Sikh treaty with Lord Lake. Architecturally the complex is a celebrated landmark: a beautiful white structure with a large central dome surrounded by smaller temples, said to look strikingly awesome on moonlit nights and a draw for archaeologists studying traditional architecture. A replica/model of the temple is exhibited in the pre-partition Punjab Museum at Lahore (verify).

name: Panch Mandir
town: Kapurthala (CSV town 'Jalandhar' is approximate - about 21 km away)
town_description: Kapurthala is the former princely capital of the Ahluwalia Sikh state, 21 km west of Jalandhar, famed for its French-inspired architecture (Jagatjit Palace, Moorish Mosque) and historic temples including the Panch Mandir.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~75 km from Kapurthala); Adampur domestic airport is closer (verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City Junction (Delhi-Amritsar line) is the main railhead, about 21 km away; Kapurthala has its own smaller station (verify).
travel.road: Kapurthala is on the Jalandhar-Amritsar corridor; regular buses and taxis run from Jalandhar (21 km).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather.
